turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll explore the repo structure and search for streaming-related code.Good, found the Responses API. Now let's check chat/completions.ts and lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts, lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts, lib/AssistantStream.ts.Now let's find where `Stream.fromSSEResponse` is actually invoked at the transport layer (likely `core/resource.ts` or `client.ts` response parsing).This confirms the low-level routing point. Now let's check `Stream.fromSSEResponse` and `_iterSSEMessages` in `core/streaming.ts` for the actual SSE parsing implementation.I have enough evidence to give a complete answer now.Now I have a complete picture. Here's the answer.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Transport/protocol layer — the actual SSE parsing:**
- `src/core/streaming.ts` — the `Stream<Item>` class (`fromSSEResponse`, `_iterSSEMessages`, `SSEDecoder`). This is the low-level `AsyncIterable` that reads the raw HTTP response body, splits it into SSE frames, and JSON-parses each `data:` line into typed events. Every streaming endpoint ultimately produces one of these.
- `src/internal/parse.ts` (`defaultParseResponse`, lines ~24-44) — the dispatch point. When a request is made with `options.stream` truthy, this function calls either a custom `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (used for higher-level wrappers) or falls back to `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` directly. This is the single chokepoint where "is this a streaming request" gets resolved into an actual stream object, called from `src/client.ts`'s core request pipeline.

**Higher-level "ergonomic" stream helpers (built on top of `Stream`):**
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — base class (`EventStream<EventTypes>`) providing `.on()`, `.emit()`, async-iterator support, abort handling. Shared by the two helpers below.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream` class (`createResponse` static factory), for the Responses API's ergonomic `.stream()` helper; accumulates deltas into a final `Response` via `accumulateResponse` (`src/lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts`).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` class (`createChatCompletion` static factory), accumulates `ChatCompletionChunk` deltas into a final `ChatCompletion` (`finalizeChatCompletion`).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner`, extends the above for the tool-calling "runner" loop (`.runTools()` with `stream: true`).
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` class (`createAssistantStream`, `createToolAssistantStream`), for the (deprecated) Assistants/Threads/Runs streaming API — also built on `EventStream` and consumes a raw `core/streaming.ts` `Stream`.

**Separate mechanism (not SSE):** `src/resources/realtime/` and `src/beta/realtime/` implement realtime streaming over WebSockets (`internal/ws.ts`, `internal/ws-adapter*.ts`), a distinct transport from the SSE-based `Stream` class.

## Public API methods that route into it

| Method | File | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-123` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | same file, ~135-169 | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | same file, ~201-206 | `ResponseStream` (ergonomic wrapper) |
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | same file, ~221-226 | `ChatCompletionStream` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true})` | same file, ~195-215 | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-44` | `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` / `.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:45-95` | `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` / `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:31-50` | `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` / `.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:60-83, 251-273` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, ~167-233, ~296-300 | `AssistantStream` |

In every non-ergonomic case, `create`/`retrieve` pass `stream: body.stream ?? false` down into `this._client.post/get(...)`, which flows through `client.ts`'s request pipeline into `defaultParseResponse` (`src/internal/parse.ts`), which is what actually constructs the `Stream` object via `Stream.fromSSEResponse`.

**Not verified:** I did not read the full body of `src/client.ts`'s request method end-to-end (only grepped relevant lines), nor did I inspect `internal/decoders/line.ts` or the realtime/websocket implementation in depth — those are asserted based on imports/naming, not full code review.

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/
